notYetListed: the light fittings (392 in 97 spaces, counted by the build)
each deck fitting's parts, as its builder names them
notAboard: Below the main deck she has no main engine, gear, generator or pump yet; the main switchboard is one item of nine cubicles. What is not built is not listed.

departments.name: Deck
departments.text: The bridge and its equipment, the mooring and anchoring gear, the stern door, the cargo's securing, the life-saving and fire appliances, and what stands on her decks.

departments.name: Engine
departments.text: Her machinery, her hydraulics, her electrical installation and lighting, ventilation and piping, the alarm system, and the maintenance computer.

departments.name: Galley
departments.text: The galley, the pantries and the messes: their equipment. Little of it is built aboard yet.

systems.name: Outfit
systems.text: The room itself and its furniture: console, stand, chairs, chart table, doors, windows, linings.

systems.name: Navigation
systems.text: Finding where she is, where she heads and what is around her: radar, charts, position, heading, depth, speed, wind.

systems.name: Steering
systems.text: From the wheel, the tiller or the autopilot to the two rudders, and the rudder angle shown back.

systems.name: Propulsion control
systems.text: The two main engines, their gearboxes and the bow thruster, worked from the bridge and from either wing.

systems.name: Radio
systems.text: Distress and safety radio for sea area A1 (within VHF range of the coast), and the float-free and portable sets.

systems.name: Internal communication
systems.text: Public address and general alarm, talkback to the mooring stations and the ramp, the telephones.

systems.name: Alarm and monitoring
systems.text: What the bridge is told without asking: machinery alarms, the watch alarm, doors and ramp, the cameras.

systems.name: Fire detection and fire-fighting
systems.text: The detection loop and its panel, call points, extinguishers, the hydrant and hose.

systems.name: Navigation lights and signals
systems.text: The lanterns and their monitored panel, the whistle, the searchlight, wipers, flags and the signalling lamp.

systems.name: Lighting
systems.text: White light for work, red for the night watch, emergency lighting, the wings and the foredeck.

systems.name: Electrical distribution
systems.text: The boards on the bridge and the cable ways from them.

systems.name: Air conditioning
systems.text: The wheelhouse room unit and its condensing unit on the compass deck.

systems.name: Piping
systems.text: Compressed air to the whistle, fresh water to the window wash, the fire main, the scuppers.

systems.name: Life-saving
systems.text: Lifebuoys, lifejackets for the watch, pyrotechnics, first aid.

systems.name: Emergency power
systems.text: The emergency generator set in its own room, with what starts it, feeds it, cools it and takes its exhaust away, and the emergency switchboard it supplies.

systems.name: Stern ramp and door
systems.text: The leaf, its hinges and cylinders, its end flaps, the ten cleats that hold it shut, their switches, and the stand it is worked from.

systems.name: Cargo access hydraulics
systems.text: The power pack in the hydraulic pump room, its pumps, valves, filters and cooler, and the pipes to the stern.

systems.name: Power generation
systems.text: The three diesel generating sets in the auxiliary engine room. Not installed: their places are marked.

systems.name: Ship's office and data
systems.text: The computers she is run from and what joins them: the maintenance program on the chief engineer's computer. No network is built yet.

systems.name: Mooring and anchoring
systems.text: Windlasses, chain stoppers, mooring winches, capstans, bitts, chocks, fairleads and rope reels.

systems.name: Ventilators and air pipes
systems.text: The ventilators of the spaces below and the tanks' air pipes, on the open decks.

systems.name: Deck lighting
systems.text: Floodlights on the open decks.

systems.name: Deck outfit
systems.text: What stands on her decks beside.

systems.name: Cargo securing
systems.text: Lashing pots in the vehicle decks.

items.name: Console
items.what: The console block: 3.7 m wide on the centreline, standing free: a way 1.0 m wide runs before it in the forward bay, from one side way to the other, so that its back is reached for electrical work and maintenance. In its back each of its five bays has a service door on hinges with two quarter-turn locks; it opens to a tap on the bay's terminals: a rail of terminal blocks, the earth bar, the ship's cables up from a transit in the block's bottom, and the slotted duct by which the bay's units are wired. Over the doors a louvred vent for each bay. From aft: a stainless grab rail along its edge; a desk that slopes up 11° with two rows of flush panels on a dark field, and the three control heads in its after edge, at the hand; a level strip with the propulsion and thruster panels, each in line ahead of its levers; an upstand leaning back 20° with the displays set into it under glass, lower in the middle so that the sea is seen over it ahead of the wheel (nothing ahead of the wheel over 1.225 m, nothing else over 1.315 m: calculation JS4-402 asked 1.22 and 1.33). Below the desk a cabinet of five bays, each with two doors on hinges, a quarter-turn lock and louvres: they open to a tap, and the units that are not seen stand behind them on shelves.

items.name: Master's chair
items.what: A high-backed pilot chair in black leather at the conning position, to port of the wheel: headrest, armrests, a footrest, on a pedestal that runs on a track let into the deck and turns. A tap on its pedestal runs it aft or forward; a tap on its seat turns it.

items.name: Watch officer's chair
items.what: The second pilot chair, at the radar: like the master's, on its own track.

items.name: Chart table
items.what: The chart table against the aft wall, with three drawers for folded charts, which run out to a tap, and the chart in use on its top. She navigates on paper charts; the chart system on the console is an aid.

items.name: Bookshelf, nautical publications
items.what: Tide tables, the list of lights, the radio signals list, the signal code and the ship's own manuals, behind a fiddle rail.

items.name: Binoculars box
items.what: Two 7 × 50 binoculars in a varnished box on the console block's port end. Its lid lifts to a tap.

items.name: Stair well and rail
items.what: The head of the crew stair from the saloon, railed on its inboard side, with a self-closing gate across the top where one comes up: it opens forward, away from the well.

items.name: Watchkeeper's table
items.what: A table at the starboard side, forward of the pantry, 0.36 m broad so that the way past it to the front of the console block is 0.70 m: a top of light varnished wood with her profile engraved in it and a cup well in its corner, a drawer that runs out to a tap, the deck log under its own lamp. (It takes the place of the fold-down log desk that hung under the port window.)

items.name: Settee
items.what: A settee in black leather in the port wing, against its after wall beside the door from the open deck and under the after window, for the pilot and for whoever waits on the bridge. (It stood along the port side of the wheelhouse, where it closed the way past the console block to 0.46 m; the owner, 12 November 2026: "Move it to port wing". It is not in the wing's inboard corner: the fire hose box and the hydrant are there.)

items.name: Handrail under the sills, port
items.what: Stainless tube on brackets under the sills: from the middle of the bay round its port corner, along the cant and aft along the port side under the windows, in one length. Something to hold in a seaway while looking out. (It ended at the console block while the block stood against the front.)

items.name: Handrail under the sills, starboard
items.what: Stainless tube on brackets under the sills: from the middle of the bay round its starboard corner, along the cant and aft along the starboard side over the watchkeeper's table. It meets the port rail in a sleeve on the centreline.

items.name: Hook rail
items.what: A board of light wood with four brass hooks under the after port window, for oilskins and the watch's lifejackets.

items.name: Door, corridor to wheelhouse
items.what: The door from the crew corridor. It opens into the wheelhouse and is kept shut at night to keep the corridor's light off the glass.

items.name: Deck covering
items.what: Blue sheet vinyl on the steel deck, turned up every wall as a coved skirting; ribbed rubber mats at the helm and before the console; the two tracks the pilot chairs run on are let into it.

items.name: Deckhead lining
items.what: Strips of off-white panel running athwartships under the compass deck, a shadow gap between each two; the cable trays lie above them.

items.name: Overhead grab rail, port
items.what: A rail under the deckhead to hold on to in a seaway.

items.name: Overhead grab rail, starboard
items.what: A rail under the deckhead to hold on to in a seaway.

items.name: Overhead console
items.what: Two sloped consoles under the deckhead over the block, either side of the instruments that hang between them: the camera monitor to port, the two VHF sets to starboard. They hang above the windows' head, so that they hide nothing the glass would show.

items.name: Sun blinds
items.what: A roller blind of tinted film in a cassette at the head of each of the bay's five windows, on two guide wires. A tap draws one down, and lets it up again.

items.name: Door to the port wing
items.what: A weathertight door, hinged on its forward edge, with a glazed upper half and a 0.15 m sill. It stands opposite the starboard one: the Minato Maru's stood in the aft corner, where the boards and their locker now have the wall to themselves.

items.name: Door to the starboard wing
items.what: A weathertight door, hinged on its forward edge, with a glazed upper half and a 0.15 m sill.

items.name: Wheelhouse plating, linings and windows
items.what: The house itself: plated outside, lined inside, a forward bay with canted corners, its five windows raked 10° under an eave, and windows down both sides: glass over 224° of the horizon from the helm.

items.name: Bridge wing, port: closed in
items.what: The wing was an open deck behind a bulwark 1.1 m high. It is closed in, as open wings are when a ship is refitted: the bulwark stays, glass stands on it between steel posts (five panes forward, leaning with the wheelhouse's own, three outboard), beside the house's forward corner a weathertight door opens outward onto the gallery before the bridge, a wall with a door closes its after end, and a roof is carried out from the wheelhouse's eave to her side. One band of windows runs across her whole breadth.

items.name: Bridge wing, starboard: closed in
items.what: Closed in like the port wing: glass on the bulwark between steel posts, a wall and a door aft, a roof from the wheelhouse's eave to her side.

items.name: Radar display
items.what: The radar picture, with target tracking: the display and its keyboard at the watch officer's chair, set in the console's upstand under a hood against the daylight.

items.name: Radar processor
items.what: The radar's processor unit: it takes the scanner's signal, the heading and the position, and gives the picture to the display and to the chart system.

items.name: Radar scanner
items.what: An X-band scanner on the mast platform: a turning unit and a 1.8 m array, 14.2 m above the waterline.

items.name: AIS transponder
items.what: Sends her name, position, course and speed on VHF and shows the ships that send theirs.

items.name: Electronic chart system
items.what: Her position on an electronic chart, with the radar's and the AIS's targets laid over it. An aid: the paper chart on the chart table is the chart she is navigated on.

items.name: GPS navigator
items.what: Position, course and speed over the ground from the satellites; it gives them to every set that needs them, the radios among them.

items.name: Echo sounder
items.what: The depth under the keel, drawn as a trace, with a shallow-water alarm.

items.name: Speed log
items.what: The speed through the water from a sensor in the bottom; shown on the conning display.

items.name: Navigation data distributor
items.what: Takes each sensor's sentences once and gives a buffered copy to every listener, so that no set can pull another's line down.

items.name: Conning display
items.what: Heading, rudder angle, both engines' revolutions, speed, depth and wind on one screen in front of the master's chair.

items.name: Satellite compass processor
items.what: Works out her true heading and rate of turn from the two antennas in the dome on the compass deck. It is the heading every set steers and plots by.

items.name: Autopilot control unit
items.what: Sets and holds a heading; it steers through the steering control unit like the wheel does.

items.name: Wind display
items.what: Wind direction and speed relative to the ship: a round instrument hung under the deckhead ahead of the helm.

items.name: Heading repeater, overhead
items.what: Her true heading on a compass card, hung under the deckhead ahead of the helm where the whole bridge reads it.

items.name: Bridge clock
items.what: A quartz clock on ship's time, hung under the deckhead. Its own battery.

items.name: Navigation network switch
items.what: The Ethernet switch of the navigation network.

items.name: Compass periscope
items.what: The magnetic compass on the compass deck, read from the helm through a tube and a mirror: it stands directly under the binnacle.

items.name: Bearing repeater, port wing
items.what: A heading repeater under an azimuth ring on a pelorus stand, to take bearings from the wing.

items.name: Bearing repeater, starboard wing
items.what: A heading repeater under an azimuth ring on a pelorus stand, to take bearings from the wing.

items.name: Ship's clock
items.what: A brass bulkhead clock over the chart table.

items.name: Barometer
items.what: An aneroid barometer.

items.name: Clinometer
items.what: Shows her list in degrees.

items.name: AIS antenna
items.what: The AIS's own VHF whip, 1.4 m.

items.name: GPS antenna
items.what: The GPS navigator's antenna dome.

items.name: Satellite compass antenna
items.what: Two satellite antennas in one dome, a known distance apart along her length: the heading is the direction from one to the other.

items.name: Magnetic compass and binnacle
items.what: The standard compass, on the centreline clear of steel and wiring, with a dimmed lamp. It needs no power to point.

items.name: AIS position antenna
items.what: A small satellite antenna for the AIS's own position fix.

items.name: Wind sensor
items.what: A cup anemometer and a vane at the starboard end of the flag yard.

items.name: Steering stand and wheel
items.what: The helm: an eight-spoke wheel on a stand. The wheel's shaft runs through a flanged bearing into the helm unit on the stand's top, where it turns two transmitters, one for each control system, and the pointer on the unit's lid that shows the rudder ordered. Where the wheel is put, the rudders follow: four degrees of wheel for one of rudder, and the spoke with the brass cap upright when they are amidships. On the page the wheel turns with the rudder.

items.name: Steering control system No. 1
items.what: The first of two control systems that have nothing in common. It compares the rudder ordered (by the wheel's first transmitter, or the autopilot) with the angle fed back from the gear and works the valves of power unit No. 1. Its supply comes from that power unit's own circuit in the steering-gear room, and its cables go down the port side.

items.name: Steering control system No. 2
items.what: The second control system: the wheel's second transmitter, its own amplifier, the valves of power unit No. 2, a supply from that unit's circuit (which comes by the emergency switchboard), and cables down the starboard side. Either system steers her alone; the selector on the stand chooses.

items.name: Steering mode selector and tiller
items.what: Chooses the control system (No. 1 or No. 2) and hand steering, autopilot or the tiller. The tiller works the valves of the chosen power unit directly (non-follow-up): the rudders move while it is held over, and it needs neither amplifier. It stands in a gate, a slot across the ship; a tap holds it over or lets it go.

items.name: Heading repeater
items.what: The heading in figures, low on the stand's face: read by looking down, not through it.

items.name: Rudder angle indicator, overhead
items.what: The rudders' true angle, from the transmitter on the steering gear: a round instrument hung under the deckhead, read from anywhere in the wheelhouse.

items.name: Rudder angle indicator, console
items.what: A second indicator among the propulsion instruments. It sits on the console, not on a stand-off, so that the sea is seen over it (calculation JS4-402).

items.name: Engine control lever, port
items.what: One lever for the port engine: ahead or astern through the gearbox, then revolutions. It stands in the desk's after edge, at the hand, and its panel and the engine instruments are read over it. A control head: the lever turns on a shaft inside the housing and comes up through a slot in its top plate; a drum on the shaft closes the slot under it, and where the arm crosses the plate is its reading on the scale beside it, from full astern through stop to full ahead. Pushed forward is ahead. A tap moves it a notch, and the port engine's lever on each wing moves with it.

items.name: Engine control lever, starboard
items.what: One lever for the starboard engine, a control head like the port one's. A tap moves it a notch, and its fellow on each wing moves with it.

items.name: Bow thruster lever
items.what: Thrust to port or starboard from the tunnel thruster in the bow. A control head whose slot lies across the ship: the lever is pushed the way her bow is to go. A tap moves it a notch, with its fellow on each wing.

items.name: Propulsion control panel
items.what: Which station has control (bridge, a wing, or the engine control room), engine start and stop, and an emergency stop for each engine under a flap. On the level strip, in line ahead of the two engine levers and under their instruments.

items.name: Bow thruster panel
items.what: Start, stop, running lamp and the motor's current. On the level strip, in line ahead of the thruster lever.

items.name: Engine instrument panel
items.what: Revolutions of both engines, their oil pressure and cooling-water temperature. Low on the console, straight ahead of the wheel: the sea is seen over it (calculation JS4-402).

items.name: Propulsion control unit, bridge
items.what: Reads the levers at the three stations, decides which one commands, and sends the orders to the engine room over two CAN lines.

items.name: Wing control station, port
items.what: Engine and thruster levers at the hand, and over them, in an upright face that leans back to the eye, a rudder angle indicator and a revolution indicator, each in line ahead of the lever it answers and read over it; at the outboard forward corner of the wing, for berthing port side to. The levers are outboard: standing at them she is seen along her side, and across the bow past the house to 45° on the other side.

items.name: Wing control station, starboard
items.what: Engine and thruster levers at the hand, and over them, in an upright face, a rudder angle indicator and a revolution indicator read over the levers; at the outboard forward corner of the wing, for berthing starboard side to. The levers are outboard, as on the port wing.

items.name: VHF radiotelephone No. 1, with DSC
items.what: The distress and calling set: 25 W, digital selective calling on channel 70 with her position from the GPS. In the starboard overhead console, with its handset in a cradle beside it on a coiled cord: the handset lifts to a tap.

items.name: VHF radiotelephone No. 2
items.what: The second set, for port and working channels, and the spare for the first: in the starboard overhead console.

items.name: NAVTEX receiver
items.what: Prints navigational and weather warnings broadcast on 518 kHz: on a bracket on the after wall over the chart table, where the warnings are plotted.

items.name: Portable VHF sets and charger
items.what: Three waterproof two-way sets for the survival craft, kept charged in their rack.

items.name: Radar transponder, port
items.what: A search and rescue transponder beside the port door, to be taken into a survival craft: it answers a searching radar. Its own battery.

items.name: Radar transponder, starboard
items.what: The second transponder, beside the starboard door. Its own battery.

items.name: Float-free EPIRB
items.what: A satellite distress beacon in a bracket that lets it go and float free if she sinks. Its own battery.

items.name: VHF antenna No. 1
items.what: A 3 m whip on the starboard side.

items.name: VHF antenna No. 2
items.what: A 3 m whip on the port side.

items.name: NAVTEX antenna
items.what: A short active antenna for 518 kHz.

items.name: Public address and general alarm amplifier
items.what: A 240 W amplifier with the general alarm's tone generator: seven short blasts and a long one on every loudspeaker aboard.

items.name: Public address and talkback panel
items.what: The microphone, the zone keys (car deck, saloon, crew, open decks), the general alarm key, and the talkback keys for the two wings, the mooring stations, the ramp and the engine control room.

items.name: Telephone
items.what: The ship's automatic telephone: cabins, mess, galley, engine control room. Its handset lies in a cradle beside it on a coiled cord, and lifts to a tap.

items.name: Sound-powered telephone
items.what: Speaks to the engine control room and the steering-gear room with no supply at all: the voice makes the current, and a hand crank rings the other end. A cased wall set on the console block's starboard end; its handset lifts to a tap.

items.name: General alarm push button
items.what: Sounds the general alarm from the door.

items.name: Loudspeaker, wheelhouse
items.what: A loudspeaker in the deckhead.

items.name: Talkback station, port wing
items.what: A weatherproof loudspeaking station on the house side, under the forward window's sill (the window was carried forward where it hung, and the door to the gallery stands at the corner).

items.name: Talkback station, starboard wing
items.what: A weatherproof loudspeaking station on the house side.

items.name: Loudhailer
items.what: A horn loudspeaker on the mast platform, for hailing and for the fog signal's listening watch.

items.name: Machinery alarm panel
items.what: The engine room's alarms in groups, with a buzzer: the bridge sees that something is wrong below, and whether the engineer has accepted it.

items.name: Bridge watch alarm
items.what: Asks the watch to press a button every few minutes at night. Unanswered, it calls the master's cabin, then the general alarm.

items.name: Watch alarm reset, chart table
items.what: A reset button at the chart table.

items.name: Camera monitor
items.what: Four cameras on one screen: the bow ramp, the car deck, the stern and the engine room.

items.name: Ramp, hatch and watertight door panel
items.what: A lamp for the bow ramp, each hatch and each of the five watertight doors: green when shut and secured, red when not.

items.name: Camera recorder
items.what: Records the cameras.

items.name: Fire detection panel
items.what: The addressable fire detection panel: it names the detector that has answered, sounds the bells, and after two minutes unaccepted, the general alarm. It has a standby battery of its own.

items.name: Manual call point
items.what: Break the glass to give the alarm.

items.name: Smoke detector
items.what: An optical smoke detector on loop 1.

items.name: Sprinkler head, port
items.what: A pendent sprinkler head in the deckhead: its glass bulb bursts at 68 °C and lets the water out. The sprinkler main it stands on is not registered yet.

items.name: Sprinkler head, starboard
items.what: A pendent sprinkler head in the deckhead. The sprinkler main it stands on is not registered yet.

items.name: Fire extinguisher, CO₂ 5 kg
items.what: For the electrical equipment: carbon dioxide leaves nothing behind.

items.name: Fire extinguisher, powder 6 kg
items.what: Dry powder, beside the port door.

items.name: Fire hose box
items.what: A 15 m hose with a dual-purpose nozzle, coiled in its box beside the hydrant.

items.name: Navigation light panel
items.what: A switch, a fuse and a lamp-failure indicator for each lantern, on a mimic of the ship; a change-over switch between its two supplies. On the console block's apron, under the desk.

items.name: Sidelight, port
items.what: Red, from right ahead to 22.5° abaft the port beam: on the wing's roof at its outer end (it stood on the bulwark's rail while the wing was open), with a screen board inboard of it.

items.name: Sidelight, starboard
items.what: Green, from right ahead to 22.5° abaft the starboard beam: on the wing's roof at its outer end, with a screen board inboard of it.

items.name: Masthead light
items.what: White, over 225° ahead, on the front of the mast above the radar, its lens clear over the posts of the radar platform.

items.name: Anchor light
items.what: White, all round, on the crown of the mast.

items.name: Stern light
items.what: White, over 135° astern: on the centreline at the stern, on the bulwark's rail over the stern door, with a screen forward of it so that it is not seen from forward of the beam.

items.name: Not-under-command lights, upper pair
items.what: Red, all round: two heights of them in a vertical line, 2 m apart, say she cannot keep out of the way. Each height is a pair of lanterns, one either side of the mast, lit together: a single lantern beside the mast would be hidden by it over 35° of the horizon, and no more than 6° is allowed.

items.name: Not-under-command lights, lower pair
items.what: Red, all round: the lower pair, 2 m under the upper.

items.name: Whistle
items.what: Two air horns on the front of the mast, sounded by compressed air.

items.name: Whistle panel
items.what: A push button for the whistle and a timer for the fog signal (one long blast every two minutes when under way).

items.name: Searchlight control
items.what: A joystick that turns and tilts the searchlight, and its lamp switch.

items.name: Wiper and window wash panel
items.what: Each wiper on, off or intermittent, and the wash. A tap on a switch turns it a step, and its wiper runs.

items.name: Window wiper, starboard
items.what: A pendulum wiper on the outside of the starboard cant's glass, hung from its spindle in the window's head under the eave; its motor is inside, over the blind. A tap starts and stops it.

items.name: Window wiper, centre
items.what: A pendulum wiper on the outside of the glass ahead of the wheel, hung from its spindle in the window's head under the eave; its motor is inside, over the blind. A tap starts and stops it.

items.name: Window wiper, port
items.what: A pendulum wiper on the outside of the port cant's glass, hung from its spindle in the window's head under the eave; its motor is inside, over the blind. A tap starts and stops it.

items.name: Clear-view screen, port
items.what: A glass disc spinning in a ring in the window ahead of the master's chair: spray and rain are thrown off it, and it is clear where the window is tinted. Its motor is at its middle, carried by a tube from the rail under the window. A tap starts and stops it.

items.name: Clear-view screen, starboard
items.what: The second clear-view screen, in the window ahead of the watch officer's chair.

items.name: Window heating junction box
items.what: Where the forward windows' heated glass is fed and switched: a box let into the lining below the sill of the starboard cant, with its lamp.

items.name: Searchlight
items.what: A 1 kW searchlight on the compass deck, turned from the console.

items.name: Flag locker
items.what: The signal flags of the international code, each rolled in its own pigeonhole.

items.name: Daylight signalling lamp
items.what: A hand lamp for Morse by day, on its hook beside the starboard door with its socket.

items.name: Deckhead light
items.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

items.name: Deckhead light
items.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

items.name: Deckhead light
items.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

items.name: Deckhead light
items.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

items.name: Deckhead light
items.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

items.name: Deckhead light
items.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

items.name: Deckhead light
items.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

items.name: Deckhead light
items.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

items.name: Chart lamp
items.what: A dimmed lamp on a stalk, red or white, that lights the chart and nothing else.

items.name: Night light, red, port
items.what: A red light over the console: enough to find a switch by, without spoiling the night vision.

items.name: Night light, red, starboard
items.what: A red light over the console.

items.name: Emergency light
items.what: Lights by itself when the main supply fails.

items.name: Transitional light
items.what: A 24 V lamp on the general service battery: it lights at once when the supply fails, before the emergency generator has started.

items.name: Wing light, port
items.what: A bulkhead light on the house side, over the forward window (the window was carried forward under where it hung, and the door to the gallery stands at the corner: nothing is built over a window).

items.name: Wing light, starboard
items.what: A bulkhead light on the house side.

items.name: Dimmer panel
items.what: Dims the instruments, the red night lights over the console and the chart lamp. A tap on a knob turns it a step: the night lights and the chart lamp go out and come on with it, and the displays darken when the instruments are turned down.

items.name: Foredeck floodlight, port
items.what: Lights the car deck forward and the ramp.

items.name: Foredeck floodlight, starboard
items.what: Lights the car deck forward and the ramp.

items.name: Wheelhouse distribution board BD1
items.what: 230 V, from the lighting board in the engine control room: eight ways for the bridge's general services.

items.name: Emergency distribution board BD2
items.what: 230 V, from the emergency switchboard: six ways for what must not go dark.

items.name: 24 V DC panel DC1, navigation and control
items.what: 24 V from the general service battery: fifteen fused ways, a voltmeter and an earth-fault lamp.

items.name: 24 V DC panel DC2, radio
items.what: 24 V from the radio battery: five fused ways, a voltmeter and the charger-failure alarm.

items.name: Sockets below the sill, port
items.what: A double 230 V socket in the lining below the sill of the port cant.

items.name: Console socket
items.what: A 230 V socket on the console block's apron.

items.name: Console heaters
items.what: Small heaters low in the console that keep the damp out of the electronics when she lies cold.

items.name: Pantry unit
items.what: A low unit under the starboard side window, wholly below its sill: the cooler in its after bay, the coffee maker in a niche with a rail across it for when she rolls, and under the niche a cupboard with the mugs, the coffee, the tea and the sugar. The cupboard opens to a tap.

items.name: Cooler
items.what: A 45-litre refrigerator for the watch: two wire shelves, a shelf in the door. It opens to a tap.

items.name: Coffee maker
items.what: A filter coffee maker with a glass jug on a hot plate: a litre and a quarter, a pot for the watch. A tap on its switch starts it, and the jug fills; a tap on the jug lifts and pours it, and it empties.

items.name: Pantry sockets
items.what: A double 230 V socket at the back of the pantry's niche, for the coffee maker and the cooler.

items.name: Cable transit at the mast
items.what: Where the cables to the mast and the compass deck pass the deck, sealed gastight and watertight.

items.name: Cable duct on the port mullion
items.what: A covered duct down a mullion of the bay and the lining under it, from the trays over the deckhead to a cable transit in the deck at its foot: the cables cross under the deck and come up into the console block, which stands free, through a transit in its bottom.

items.name: Cable duct on the starboard mullion
items.what: A covered duct down a mullion of the bay and the lining under it, from the trays over the deckhead to a cable transit in the deck at its foot: the cables cross under the deck and come up into the console block, which stands free, through a transit in its bottom.

items.name: Air conditioner, room unit
items.what: The wheelhouse's cooling and dehumidifying unit, high on the aft wall over the stair.

items.name: Air conditioner, condensing unit
items.what: The compressor and condenser, on the compass deck above the room unit.

items.name: Fire hydrant, port wing
items.what: A 50 mm hydrant on the fire main, with a hose coupling and a hand valve.

items.name: Scupper, port wing
items.what: The wing's deck drain, led overboard.

items.name: Scupper, starboard wing
items.what: The wing's deck drain, led overboard.

items.name: Whistle valve
items.what: The valve that lets air to the whistle: opened by a solenoid from the push buttons and the fog timer, or by hand with the pull above the helm.

items.name: Window wash valve
items.what: A solenoid valve on the fresh-water line to the wash nozzles.

items.name: Window wash nozzles
items.what: A brass pipe round the bay's head outside, under the eave, with a jet over each wiper's glass.

items.name: Lifebuoy with light and smoke, port
items.what: A lifebuoy on a quick-release with a self-igniting light and a smoke float: thrown from the wing for a man overboard.

items.name: Lifebuoy with light and smoke, starboard
items.what: A lifebuoy on a quick-release with a self-igniting light and a smoke float.

items.name: Locker: lifejackets and pyrotechnics
items.what: Four lifejackets for the watch, twelve parachute flares and the line-throwing appliance, under the boards.

items.name: First-aid kit
items.what: A first-aid box under the flag locker.

items.name: Emergency generator set No. 1
items.what: A six-cylinder turbocharged diesel and its alternator on one skid, on six rubber mounts: 440 V, three-phase, 60 Hz, 500 kW on the owner's drawing. Its radiator stands at its forward end in a cowl, so it needs no sea water. It starts by itself when the main board is dead.

items.name: Starting battery bank, 24 V
items.what: Eight 12 V blocks in a steel rack, in two strings: they turn the starter, and nothing else is fed from them. The ship's transitional and radio batteries are not in this room.

items.name: Starting battery charger
items.what: Keeps the starting bank charged from the emergency switchboard; a voltmeter, an ammeter and a failure lamp.

items.name: Emergency generator control panel
items.what: Starts and stops the set, by itself or by hand; shows its voltage, frequency, load, oil pressure and temperature; the emergency stop is on its front. Fed from the starting battery.

items.name: Emergency switchboard, 440 V
items.what: Two sections: the generator breaker and the bus tie from the main board with their meters; and the ways to what must work when all else has stopped (steering, the emergency fire pump, emergency lighting, navigation lights, radio, alarms, the bilge pump).

items.name: Day tank, about 200 L
items.what: The set's own fuel, high enough to run to the engine by gravity: on a stand over a tray, with a level gauge, filled from the service tank.

items.name: Fuel quick-closing valve and its pull
items.what: Under the tank: shut by a wire from the red box outside the door, so that nobody goes into a fire to stop the fuel.

items.name: Exhaust: bellows, lagged riser, silencer
items.what: From the turbocharger through a bellows and a lagged riser up through the deckhead to a silencer on the roof.

items.name: Supply air duct and fire damper FD-01
items.what: Air for the engine and the room, in through a louvre on the forward wall; the damper shuts it. Its lever is worked by hand: tap it.

items.name: Exhaust air duct and fire damper FD-02
items.what: The room's warm air, out through a louvre on the starboard wall; the damper shuts it. Its lever is worked by hand: tap it.

items.name: Fuel lines
items.what: Supply from the day tank to the engine's filters and the return beside it, each tagged; the filling line from the service tank with its strainer and valve; the tank's vent, out through the wall.

items.name: Emergency generator room light No. 1
items.what: A fitting under the deckhead beams. Two of the four are on the emergency lighting: the one before the switchboard and the one over the way to the door.

items.name: Emergency generator room light No. 2
items.what: A fitting under the deckhead beams. Two of the four are on the emergency lighting: the one before the switchboard and the one over the way to the door.

items.name: Emergency generator room light No. 3
items.what: A fitting under the deckhead beams. Two of the four are on the emergency lighting: the one before the switchboard and the one over the way to the door.

items.name: Emergency generator room light No. 4
items.what: A fitting under the deckhead beams. Two of the four are on the emergency lighting: the one before the switchboard and the one over the way to the door.

items.name: Fire extinguisher, CO2 5 kg, emergency generator room
items.what: Carbon dioxide, for a fire in the switchboard or the set: by the door, under its sign.

items.name: Manual call point, emergency generator room
items.what: Break the glass to give the alarm: by the door one leaves by.

items.name: Heat detector, emergency generator room
items.what: A heat detector on loop 1 (a running diesel would set a smoke detector off).

items.name: Telephone, emergency generator room
items.what: To the wheelhouse and the engine control room.

items.name: Weathertight door, emergency generator room (house top)
items.what: A steel door with a porthole, two dogs and a lever handle, opening outward onto the deck: the escape route ends at it.

items.name: Stern ramp and door
items.what: One leaf, 11 m long and 9.4 m wide, a box girder 0.42 m deep, about 55 t. Raised, it is the stern door: it lies against a rubber seal round the opening; ten cleats hold it, and a safety latch on each door post that needs no oil. It turns on six hinges at the sill and lowers aft onto the quay: level at 90 degrees, and 4 degrees further for a quay that lies lower. Clear driveway 8 m, between the two cylinders.

items.name: Ramp hinges
items.what: Six along the sill: at each a lug of the ship stands out of the transom into a slot in the leaf's foot, and one pin of 90 mm goes through all of them. The hinge line lies 45 mm abaft the transom and 15 mm under the main deck, so that the roadway comes down level with the deck.

items.name: Ramp cylinder, port
items.what: Double-acting, bore 300 mm, rod 170 mm, stroke 3.40 m. Hung from a bracket under the upper deck's web beam at 3.6 m and pinned to a lug on the leaf 2.2 m from the hinge: 4.73 m between its pins with the ramp raised, 7.87 m with it level. It pulls: at most 952 kN, 198 bar on its rod side. A load-holding valve is bolted to it: if a hose bursts the ramp stays where it is.

items.name: Ramp cylinder, starboard
items.what: Double-acting, bore 300 mm, rod 170 mm, stroke 3.40 m. Hung from a bracket under the upper deck's web beam at 3.6 m and pinned to a lug on the leaf 2.2 m from the hinge: 4.73 m between its pins with the ramp raised, 7.87 m with it level. It pulls: at most 952 kN, 198 bar on its rod side. A load-holding valve is bolted to it: if a hose bursts the ramp stays where it is.

items.name: End flaps
items.what: 8 flaps of 1.1 by 1.2 m across the ramp's end, each on its own hinge: they lie on the quay and take up her list. Stowed, they lie folded back over the roadway; they fold out as the ramp comes down.

items.name: Door seal
items.what: A rubber strip on the transom round the opening's sides and head: the raised ramp is drawn against it by the cleats. The roadway is left flat where it meets it.

items.name: Bolt cleat, port, No. 1
items.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 0.7 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

items.name: Bolt cleat, port, No. 2
items.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 1.5 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

items.name: Bolt cleat, port, No. 3
items.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 3.3 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

items.name: Bolt cleat, port, No. 4
items.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 4.4 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

items.name: Bolt cleat, starboard, No. 1
items.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 0.7 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

items.name: Bolt cleat, starboard, No. 2
items.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 1.5 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

items.name: Bolt cleat, starboard, No. 3
items.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 3.3 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

items.name: Bolt cleat, starboard, No. 4
items.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 4.4 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

items.name: Hook cleat, port
items.what: At the door's head: an arm on a pivot under a hanger, with a tooth that stands up abaft a pin on the ramp. To let go, its cylinder drops the arm 35 degrees. A switch on it says when it is home.

items.name: Hook cleat, starboard
items.what: At the door's head: an arm on a pivot under a hanger, with a tooth that stands up abaft a pin on the ramp. To let go, its cylinder drops the arm 35 degrees. A switch on it says when it is home.

items.name: Ramp control stand
items.what: A steel desk on the main deck beside the door, port side, against the mooring station's wall: whoever works it stands inboard of it with the ramp's foot at the left hand. On the desk: the emergency stop, a start and a stop button for each main pump, and two spring-centred levers, CLEATS (lock, open) and RAMP (raise, lower). On the upstand: two pressure indicators, 0 to 250 bar (SYSTEM: the pumps' pressure; RAMP LINE A: what carries the leaf, 189 bar with it level), eight lamp windows (power on, pump 1 running, pump 2 running, ramp closed, cleats locked, cleats open, oil level, oil temperature), the key switch that gives the control to the stand or to the bridge, lamp test, horn, and the instructions engraved. Interlocked: no lever does anything until a pump runs; the ramp is not lowered until the cleats are open; the cleats are not locked until the ramp is home; the emergency stop trips both pumps and holds the ramp. A beacon on its top is lit while the ramp is neither locked nor landed. Its door opens on the terminals of X1.

items.name: Junction box of the ramp's switches
items.what: On the port mooring station's wall behind the control stand: the ten cleats' switches, the two latches' and the two door switches are joined here to the stand, to the bridge's door and ramp panel and to the alarm system.

items.name: Door switch, port
items.what: On the door post: closed by the raised ramp when it is home against its seal. With the ten cleats' and the two latches' switches it makes "ramp closed and locked".

items.name: Door switch, starboard
items.what: On the door post: closed by the raised ramp when it is home against its seal. With the ten cleats' and the two latches' switches it makes "ramp closed and locked".

items.name: Safety latch, port
items.what: On the door post at breast height. It needs no oil to hold: an arm on a pivot whose tooth falls by its own weight behind a striker pin on the ramp as the ramp comes home, and stays there. It is lifted 30 degrees to let the ramp go, by a small cylinder on the cleats' let-go line or, with no oil, by pressing down its handle; a pin through arm and bracket secures it for the sea passage. It lets go first and falls in last. A switch on it says when it is home.

items.name: Safety latch, starboard
items.what: On the door post at breast height. It needs no oil to hold: an arm on a pivot whose tooth falls by its own weight behind a striker pin on the ramp as the ramp comes home, and stays there. It is lifted 30 degrees to let the ramp go, by a small cylinder on the cleats' let-go line or, with no oil, by pressing down its handle; a pin through arm and bracket secures it for the sea passage. It lets go first and falls in last. A switch on it says when it is home.

items.name: Stern ramp power pack (HPU-R)
items.what: A tank of about 1,500 litres on a drip tray, with the two main pumps and the cleats' pump on its lid, a breather and filler, level and temperature switches. Oil: ISO VG 46, mineral hydraulic oil of high viscosity index, type HVLP (DIN 51524 part 3; ISO 11158 class HV); filled to 1,260 litres with the ramp raised. On its inboard side a level glass with an engraved scale (FILL; RAMP DOWN; LOW, where OIL LEVEL is given; STOP, under which no pump is run): the oil in it falls 9 cm as the ramp is lowered, because the cylinders' rods take their own volume out of the tank, and comes back as it is raised. Beside it a dial thermometer: the oil works at 30 to 55 degrees, OIL TEMP is given at 70. It works the stern ramp and its cleats; the ramp cover over the fixed ramp is to be worked from it too. Operating instruction: JS3-304-M1.

items.name: Main pump No. 1
items.what: An axial piston pump of variable delivery under a 37 kW motor on the tank's lid: its pressure compensator holds 195 bar, and it delivers what the valves ask for, up to 100 l/min; with every valve in its middle it holds the pressure and delivers nothing. One pump works the ramp at half speed. Its delivery goes through a non-return valve into the pressure block.

items.name: Main pump No. 2
items.what: As No. 1. With both running the ramp is raised from its lowest in about a minute and a half.

items.name: Cleat pump
items.what: A small pump under a 4 kW motor: it works the ten cleats, so that they can be locked and let go with the main pumps stopped. It delivers into a block of its own on the lid, with the cleats' relief valve RV2 (160 bar) on it; line S goes from there to the cleat valve.

items.name: Oil cooler
items.what: An air-blast cooler on the tank's after end: the return line comes down into it and goes on from its other end to the return filter. Its 1.1 kW fan runs from 45 degrees of oil until it is back at 40.

items.name: Pressure block
items.what: On the tank's lid: the two main pumps' deliveries come into it, each through its non-return valve; on it the pressure filter, the relief valve set to 210 bar, and the system's gauge on its gauge cock. Line P leaves its top for the valve stand.

items.name: Return filter
items.what: On the lid: the return comes into it from the cooler and goes through it into the tank. 25 micron, with a clogging indicator.

items.name: Hand pump
items.what: On the tank's inboard side: with no power the cleats and, slowly, the ramp are worked by it through the same valves.

items.name: Valve stand
items.what: On the inboard wall: three lever valves with solenoids (the ramp, the cleats, and one for the ramp cover), each worked from the control stand or here by hand (the ramp's and the cleats' levers work on the page: a pump must run); a gauge on a gauge cock for each of the ramp's two lines; a marker on each of the eight lines that leave its top, with its letter and what it does, and two pressure transmitters (PT1 the system, PT2 line A) for the control stand's indicators. The cleats must be free before the ramp's valve can lower it.

items.name: Stern ramp starter panel (RSP)
items.what: On the hydraulic pump room's forward wall. Its door opens on the isolator, the two star-delta starters, the two direct starters, the control transformer and the terminals.

items.name: Main switchboard, 690 V
items.what: Nine cubicles in a row 4.5 m long, looking aft into the aisle: two bus sections with a tie and a separate thruster bus, 1600 A bars, 690 V, 60 Hz. From outboard: 1 SG2 (1000 A); 2 DG3 (400 A); 3 DG2 (400 A); 4 T2 (800 A); 5 TIE (1600 A); 6 T1 (800 A); 7 DG1 (400 A); 8 SG1 (1000 A); 9 BT (800 A). Each has its instruments, its air circuit breaker and, behind the lower door (it opens to a tap), the three bars its cables are landed on: every cable comes up through its gland in the platform, is cleated, and has its number on a tag. The generating sets, the shaft generators, the transformers and the thruster are not installed: the board is dead, and its cables end at their glands. The 440 V and 230 V sections, which face it, are drawn (JS8-865 sheet 2) and not built.

items.name: PSB: place marked
items.what: NOT INSTALLED. Main switchboard, 440 V section: behind the two transformers; her motors other than the thruster. The stern ramp's feeder ends here. Its place is marked on the floor (4.50 by 0.80 m) with a sign, and the cables that are to be landed on it end here, tagged.

items.name: T1: place marked
items.what: NOT INSTALLED. Main transformer No. 1, 690/440 V, 800 kVA: either of the two carries the whole 440 V load. Its place is marked on the floor (1.05 by 1.10 m) with a sign, and the cables that are to be landed on it end here, tagged.

items.name: T2: place marked
items.what: NOT INSTALLED. Main transformer No. 2, 690/440 V, 800 kVA. Its place is marked on the floor (1.05 by 1.10 m) with a sign, and the cables that are to be landed on it end here, tagged.

items.name: DG1: place marked
items.what: NOT INSTALLED. Diesel generating set No. 1: 320 kW, 400 kVA, 690 V, 60 Hz, 1,800 rpm. Alternator forward. Its place is marked on the floor (1.30 by 3.70 m) with a sign, and the cables that are to be landed on it end here, tagged.

items.name: DG2: place marked
items.what: NOT INSTALLED. Diesel generating set No. 2: 320 kW, 400 kVA, 690 V, 60 Hz, 1,800 rpm. Alternator forward. Its place is marked on the floor (1.30 by 3.70 m) with a sign, and the cables that are to be landed on it end here, tagged.

items.name: DG3: place marked
items.what: NOT INSTALLED. Diesel generating set No. 3: 320 kW, 400 kVA, 690 V, 60 Hz, 1,800 rpm. Alternator forward. Its place is marked on the floor (1.30 by 3.70 m) with a sign, and the cables that are to be landed on it end here, tagged.

items.name: Maintenance computer
items.what: The chief engineer's computer, on the desk in the day room: a screen on its stand, a keyboard, a mouse, and the system unit on the deck under the desk's after end. On it runs Maintenance Desk, a Johansson Co program: every item aboard with its jobs, its records, its drawings and its instructions. **A tap on it sits one down at it**: the program fills the page, and one button, "Back to the Chisum", goes back aboard.

items.name: Twin socket outlet, chief engineer's desk
items.what: A twin 230 V socket on her side under the desk, 0.30 m over the deck, for the computer and its screen: circuit S1 of the suite's board DB-CE (16 A, 3 x 2.5 mm², in skirting trunking, as the owner's method statement MS-CE-001 has it). Its cable goes aft and inboard in the trunking to the place of DB-CE beside the door and **ends there in a box, marked**: the board is not installed.

items.name: Data outlet, chief engineer's desk
items.what: A network outlet beside the socket. Its cable goes in the same trunking to the same box and **ends there, marked**: no network cabinet is installed aboard, and no network is registered. The maintenance program keeps its records on the computer itself and needs none.

items.name: Place of distribution board DB-CE (not installed)
items.what: On the after wall beside the door: a yellow outline and a sign where the suite's distribution board is to stand, and under it the box in which the day room's two cables end. **Nothing is installed.** The skirting trunking from the desk's outlets comes along her side and the after wall and up to the box.

items.name: Desk, chief engineer's day room
items.what: A writing desk 1.60 m long and 0.75 m deep along her side at the room's after end, as the owner's drawing of the suite has it (CE-SUITE-GA-001: at the ship's side beside a window). A top on two end panels with a back panel between them, and a pedestal of three drawers at its forward end. Its forward half metre is under the window, 0.31 m under the sill.

items.name: Chair, chief engineer's desk
items.what: An office chair on a five-star base before the desk: whoever sits in it faces her side and the screen, with the window at the right hand.

items.name: Wall calendar, chief engineer's day room
items.what: A calendar on the after wall, open at November 2026 with the day ringed: "The engine room watch", three engineers in boiler suits in a manga's manner. The owner, 12 November 2026: "a calendar in the chief engineers office with cute manga ladies". Its picture was made with an image service from a description (blender/cabin_pictures.py says how); its month is drawn from the calendar itself.

items.name: Lifeboat and davits, port
items.what: The boat deck is 3.6 m wide and more here, beside the narrow part of the house: a 7.3 m boat for 40 under gravity davits, swung out over her side; the embarkation deck is the boat deck itself

items.name: Lifeboat and davits, starboard
items.what: The boat deck is 3.6 m wide and more here, beside the narrow part of the house: a 7.3 m boat for 40 under gravity davits, swung out over her side; the embarkation deck is the boat deck itself

items.name: Liferaft, port
items.what: At the rail, where it is thrown or floats free; a metre of deck is left between it and the house's side

items.name: Liferaft, starboard
items.what: At the rail, where it is thrown or floats free; a metre of deck is left between it and the house's side

items.name: Liferaft, port
items.what: At the rail, where it is thrown or floats free; a metre of deck is left between it and the house's side

items.name: Liferaft, starboard
items.what: At the rail, where it is thrown or floats free; a metre of deck is left between it and the house's side

items.name: Liferaft, port
items.what: At the rail, where it is thrown or floats free; a metre of deck is left between it and the house's side

items.name: Liferaft, starboard
items.what: At the rail, where it is thrown or floats free; a metre of deck is left between it and the house's side

items.name: Anchor windlass and mooring winch, port
items.what: In line with its hawse pipe, whose upper end is 2.6 m before it; its chain pipe goes down forward of the collision bulkhead (110.4 m) to the chain locker; a warping head on its outboard end

items.name: Anchor windlass and mooring winch, starboard
items.what: In line with its hawse pipe, whose upper end is 2.6 m before it; its chain pipe goes down forward of the collision bulkhead (110.4 m) to the chain locker; a warping head on its outboard end

items.name: Chain stopper, port
items.what: Between the windlass and the hawse pipe: it holds the anchor at sea and the cable at anchor

items.name: Chain stopper, starboard
items.what: Between the windlass and the hawse pipe: it holds the anchor at sea and the cable at anchor

items.name: Mooring winch, port
items.what: The head and breast lines' winch, clear of the windlass and 2.8 m before the house; its line leads forward to the fairlead and out at a chock

items.name: Mooring winch, starboard
items.what: The head and breast lines' winch, clear of the windlass and 2.8 m before the house; its line leads forward to the fairlead and out at a chock

items.name: Bitts, port
items.what: For the head line, abaft its chock in the bow

items.name: Bitts, starboard
items.what: For the head line, abaft its chock in the bow

items.name: Bitts, port
items.what: For the breast line, beside its chock

items.name: Bitts, starboard
items.what: For the breast line, beside its chock

items.name: Bitts, port
items.what: For the forward spring, beside its chock

items.name: Bitts, starboard
items.what: For the forward spring, beside its chock

items.name: Roller fairlead, port
items.what: Turns a line from the windlass's warping head toward the bow chock

items.name: Roller fairlead, starboard
items.what: Turns a line from the windlass's warping head toward the bow chock
